backlog.description: Continue auditing `jotd666` repositories not yet promoted, especially candidates with missing or template/copied READMEs; require project-specific evidence before adding them.
backlog.notes: Promoted Xevious and Galaxian after project-specific README verification. Repositories with copied/mismatched READMEs (including berzerk, super_pacman, digdug, rolling_thunder, tiger_heli, bosconian and mrdo) remain unpromoted pending project-specific evidence; jungle_king and jrpacman500 lacked useful README evidence in this pass.

backlog.description: Continue mining `hitchhikr` beyond the eight promoted Amiga/ST disassemblies and follow its credited tool/predecessor links.
backlog.notes: Promoted x68k2amiga, crudNES and Oktalyzer after primary README review. Continue with remaining packer/converter/tool repositories and any additional game/application disassemblies.

backlog.description: Resolve and assess AmberWorlds / Oliver Gantert, Slothsoft / Daniel Schulz and Nico Bendlin's Amber research as possible additional tracked projects.
backlog.notes: Resolved all named predecessors from Pyrdacor's primary Ambermoon README. Amberworld was promoted as a historical RE project; Slothsoft and Nico Bendlin are indexed as credited predecessor research sources but not promoted without fuller primary project inspection. kermitfrog/Amberstar is a fork of the already tracked Pyrdacor/Amberstar and was not duplicated.

backlog.description: Continue mining Tetracorp external references and the Pyrdacor/Amber predecessor graph.
backlog.notes: Added tetracorp/tokimeki-memorial as an independent PlayStation Ghidra analysis project and resolved the Amber predecessor links; continue with Tetracorp's Amiga-focused external references.

backlog.description: Continue watching `geogeo28/atari_reverse` for newly added reverse-engineering targets.
**BLACK ICE remains excluded** because its own documentation identifies it as an original game built from knowledge gained during RE work rather than an RE project itself.

Audit `TheGoodDoktor/C64AnalyserProjects` title directories for sufficiently substantive independent binary-analysis records; preserve analysis-state projects distinctly from full source reconstructions.
Continue mining Ricardo Quesada's C64 work beyond Commando.
Continue mining C64 Mark and the wider Llamasource graph.
Enumerate additional Piddewitt reverse-engineered game-source repositories.
Treat recovered/original source collections cautiously: original source alone does not qualify unless substantial reverse engineering accompanies it.
Audit `TheGoodDoktor/SpectrumAnalyserProjects` systematically; it contains many large title-specific analysis datasets that are not yet represented individually.
backlog.notes: All substantive title directories reviewed and promoted. ZXBasic was reviewed but left unpromoted because it is an almost-empty generic analysis scaffold with no snapshot/legacy subject established.

backlog.description: Continue graph-style discovery through SkoolKit links, author profiles and references from already tracked disassemblies.
Prefer canonical/current project sources over archive mirrors, while keeping genuinely independent disassemblies as separate records.
Continue discovery through CPC Analyser users, CPCWiki/CPCRulez references, firmware/protection research and GitHub project graphs.

Audit RetroRE's untracked **Full/Partial** 6502 reverse-engineering links systematically. High-value leads include Apple II Choplifter/6502disassembly projects, BBC Micro Exile/Imogen/Thrust, Atari 2600 multi-title disassembly collections, C64 title reconstructions and NES full disassemblies; continue distinguishing original-source preservation from RE.
backlog.notes: Promoted Mega Man 3, 4, 5 and 6 from the current refreshing-lemonade repositories (the older RetroRE links used the former Raidenthequick owner). Each primary README describes the code/data disassembly as complete and a clean NTSC-U ROM rebuild with xkas-plus; byte-exact remains unset because the documentation does not explicitly say byte-for-byte identical. Continue the remaining Apple II, Atari 2600/8-bit, C64 and NES leads. Promoted seven Apple II projects from 6502disassembly.com after primary-site review: Bomber, Deathmaze 5000, Elite, Phantoms Five, Golden Voyage/Scott Adams Adventures, Space Eggs and Stellar 7. These are substantial SourceGen-backed disassembly/analysis projects, but build/runnable/byte-exact fields remain unknown because the site presents analysis project sets rather than explicitly verified reassemblies. Epoch remains a known work-in-progress lead for a later pass.

backlog.description: Mine Mark Moxon's linked archaeology graph beyond the projects already promoted, but keep original-source-only preservation distinct from binary/source reconstruction.
backlog.notes: Reviewed the main source/hack/tool graph. Promoted six distinct Elite modifications/editors; original-source-only variants and Elite Compendium repositories remain discovery context. !EliteNet was reviewed but not promoted because it is a companion scoreboard application and explicitly leaves Archimedes Elite untouched.

backlog.description: Treat newly represented platforms as first-class discovery targets rather than restricting future searches to the original five platform families.
Track core emulators, debuggers, reassemblers, reconstructed toolchains and archival development systems when they are directly useful to software archaeology or reproducible legacy development.
Keep ordinary open-source continuation/maintenance projects distinct from reverse-engineering records; they may remain discovery nodes without becoming catalogue records.
